entries.author: A
entries.text: Famous headline attractions are almost never worth the queues — the real city is in ordinary neighborhoods, and I steer people away from the landmark circuit.

entries.author: A
entries.text: The single best use of travel money is eating seriously well, and I'd happily book a cheaper room to afford memorable meals.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Tight hour-by-hour itineraries ruin trips; I plan at most one anchor activity per day and let the rest happen.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Lisbon's trams are a nightmare during peak hours.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Tram 28 is a nightmare; Tram 24E is the better alternative for the hills.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Mid-range spots in Lisbon are often overpriced tourist traps; look for 'tascas'.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Belém Tower queues are a waste of time; booking online is the only sane option.

entries.author: A
entries.text: Uber is a necessary supplement to public transport in Lisbon due to the steep hills.
